prompt.brief: Design a URL shortening service like bit.ly that creates compact links for valid destination URLs and redirects them with low, predictable latency at high read volume.
successSignals: Separate the link-creation path from the read-heavy redirect path and give each path an explicit latency and availability budget.
Choose a short-code strategy, explain its capacity and collision behavior, and make creation retries idempotent.
Keep redirect resolution cache-first and move click analytics, aggregation, and other non-critical work off the redirect path.
Cover aliases, expiration, deletion, privacy, destination safety, hot links, and degraded behavior.

functional: Create a compact short URL for a valid destination URL.
Redirect a short code to its current destination while enforcing status and expiration.
Support optional custom aliases and expiration dates.
Provide aggregate click analytics by time, referrer, device, and coarse location.
Let an authenticated owner update, disable, or delete a link.
Make create requests safe to retry with an idempotency key.
nonFunctional: Keep redirect p99 latency below 100 ms for the normal cache-first path.
Target 99.99% availability for redirects and 99.9% availability for link creation.
Make newly created links readable after the create response and keep updates ordered per link.
Make private or unlisted codes difficult to enumerate and rate-limit abuse without slowing healthy redirects.
Treat analytics as eventually consistent and never block a redirect on analytics availability.
scaleAssumptions: Create 100 million new links per month and serve 10 billion redirects per month, with sharp viral peaks.
The redirect-to-create ratio is approximately 100:1; a hot code can receive a disproportionate share of traffic.
Retain links for five years by default, or until a configured expiration date; raw click events use a separate retention policy.
Use a seven- or eight-character Base62 code space and partition durable lookups by a hash of the short code.

metrics.label: Create traffic
metrics.description: 100 million link creations per month before burst and regional capacity headroom.

metrics.label: Redirect traffic
metrics.description: 10 billion redirects per month; viral links and campaigns determine peak sizing.

metrics.label: Availability
metrics.description: The read-heavy redirect path has the stricter availability objective.

metrics.label: Redirect latency
metrics.description: The cache-first redirect budget excludes slow analytics and dashboard work.

metrics.label: Code capacity
metrics.description: Seven Base62 characters provide a large namespace; eight characters leave additional growth room.

entities.name: ShortURL
entities.notes: Authoritative link metadata and lifecycle state. The primary read is shortCode to originalUrl; owner and status indexes support management and revocation.

entities.name: ClickEvent
entities.notes: Privacy-scoped redirect telemetry emitted asynchronously after the redirect decision; it is not part of redirect correctness.

entities.name: AnalyticsAggregate
entities.notes: Rebuildable time-bucketed click totals served to dashboards with an explicit processing watermark.

entities.name: IdempotencyRecord
entities.notes: Bounded record that maps a retried create request to its original result and rejects reuse with a different payload.

apis.contract: { originalUrl, customAlias?, expiresAt?, idempotencyKey } -> { linkId, shortCode, status }
apis.notes: Validate the destination and policy, reserve a collision-free code or alias, commit link metadata, and return the existing result for a safe retry.

apis.contract: 302/301 with Location: originalUrl and cache headers
apis.notes: Resolve from edge or Redis first, fall back to the link store on a miss, enforce status and expiry, and emit click telemetry without waiting for analytics.

apis.contract: { originalUrl?, expiresAt?, status?, expectedVersion } -> { shortCode, version }
apis.notes: Authorize the owner, apply an optimistic version check, update the authoritative row, and invalidate the old redirect projection.
Write a tombstone or disabled state before invalidating caches so a deleted link cannot be recreated or served from a stale cache accidentally.
Read asynchronous click aggregates with a processing watermark rather than scanning raw redirect events.

dataFlow.title: Create and commit a short link
dataFlow.description: The gateway validates the destination, applies abuse and rate-limit policy, allocates a unique code, and commits ShortURL metadata with an idempotency record before returning success.

dataFlow.title: Prime the read path
dataFlow.description: After the durable write, the service writes or invalidates the redirect cache and returns the code only after the create result is readable from the authoritative region.

dataFlow.title: Resolve a redirect
dataFlow.description: For GET /{shortCode}, the edge or redirect cache checks status and expiry on a hit; a miss reads the link store, fills the cache, and returns a 302 by default or a 301 when the link is intentionally immutable.

dataFlow.title: Emit click telemetry asynchronously
dataFlow.description: The redirect decision returns immediately while a buffered event is sent to a durable queue; analytics workers deduplicate events and build time-bucketed aggregates.

dataFlow.title: Expire, update, or delete safely
dataFlow.description: Owner commands and lifecycle workers change the authoritative status, invalidate edge and regional caches, and retain only policy-approved link, click, and audit data.

architecture.title: URL Shortener reference architecture
architecture.summary: A cache-first redirect path keeps hot links fast, while link creation, lifecycle changes, and click analytics use durable boundaries that do not make redirects depend on slow secondary systems.

layers.label: Serving layer
layers.description: Clients, edge routing, and synchronous services that create links or resolve redirects.

layers.label: Authoritative state
layers.description: Durable link metadata and lifecycle state behind the cache-first lookup.

layers.label: Async analytics layer
layers.description: Click events are buffered and aggregated independently from redirect availability.

layers.label: Safety and operations
layers.description: SLOs, cache health, abuse signals, and queue lag are observable without joining the redirect critical path.

keyPaths.label: Link creation path
keyPaths.description: Client -> edge -> gateway -> link service -> ID generator and link store.

keyPaths.label: Redirect path
keyPaths.description: Edge -> gateway -> link service -> redirect cache, with a link-store fallback on a miss.

keyPaths.label: Click analytics path
keyPaths.description: Link service -> click queue -> analytics worker -> analytics store without waiting for aggregation.

components.label: Browsers and API clients
components.description: Owners create and manage links; browsers and crawlers follow short URLs.

components.label: Edge / CDN
components.description: Terminates connections, applies coarse protection, and serves globally cacheable hot redirects close to users.

properties.responsibility: Routing, edge caching, and DDoS protection

components.label: API gateway
components.description: Validates request shape, authenticates owners, applies quotas, and routes create, manage, and redirect traffic.

properties.protection: Authentication, URL policy, rate limits, and request size limits

components.label: URL Shortener Service
components.description: Creates codes, resolves redirects, enforces lifecycle state, and emits click events.

properties.criticalPath: Cache-first shortCode lookup with a bounded database fallback

components.label: ID and alias allocator
components.description: Reserves unique numeric IDs or custom aliases and encodes generated IDs as compact Base62 codes.

properties.strategy: Sequence or distributed unique ID plus Base62; conditional uniqueness for aliases

components.label: Redirect cache
components.description: Caches shortCode-to-destination mappings for the read-heavy path with TTLs, version metadata, and targeted invalidation.

properties.strategy: Edge plus regional cache-aside lookup; stampede protection for hot codes

components.label: Link store
components.description: Authoritative store for ShortURL metadata, ownership, status, versions, idempotency records, and expiry.

properties.accessPattern: Primary lookup by hashed shortCode with owner and expiry indexes

components.label: Click event queue
components.description: Buffers privacy-scoped redirect events so analytics outages and bursts do not take down redirects.

properties.delivery: Durable, asynchronous, and at least once

components.label: Analytics workers
components.description: Normalize click events, apply retention and privacy rules, and roll events into time buckets.

properties.output: Minute, hour, referrer, device, and coarse-location aggregates

components.label: Analytics store
components.description: Serves link-owner dashboards from rebuildable aggregates rather than scanning raw click events.

properties.dimensions: Time, device, referrer, coarse geography, and processing freshness

components.label: Reliability and abuse monitoring
components.description: Tracks redirect SLOs, cache health, store errors, code collisions, abuse decisions, and analytics lag.

properties.signals: Redirect p99, availability, cache hit rate, hot codes, errors, abuse rate, and queue lag

connections.label: HTTPS
connections.description: Create, manage, or follow a short link.

connections.label: Route
connections.description: Forward cache misses, creates, and management requests to the API layer.

connections.label: Create or resolve
connections.description: Route validated link operations to the URL Shortener Service.

connections.label: Allocate code
connections.description: Reserve a unique ID or custom alias before committing a new link.

connections.label: Cache lookup
connections.description: Read the current destination and lifecycle metadata from the cache first.

connections.label: Cache miss
connections.description: Fall back to authoritative storage, then refill the cache with the current version and expiry.

connections.label: Commit link
connections.description: Persist link metadata, lifecycle changes, and idempotency records with conditional writes.

connections.label: Click event
connections.description: Publish privacy-scoped redirect telemetry without waiting for analytics processing.

connections.label: Consume clicks
connections.description: Process click events independently from redirect traffic and deduplicate retries.

connections.label: Aggregate
connections.description: Write queryable time-bucketed aggregates and update the freshness watermark.

connections.label: SLO and abuse signals
connections.description: Emit redirect latency, cache, error, collision, lifecycle, and destination-safety telemetry.

deepDives.title: Short-code generation and collision handling
points: A sequence, Snowflake-style ID, or another unique numeric allocator can be Base62 encoded into seven or eight characters; a random opaque ID reduces enumeration but needs collision retries.

Enforce uniqueness with a database constraint or conditional write. Custom aliases should return a conflict when already reserved, and the same idempotency key should return the original create result.
Do not hash only the destination URL if two owners need separate links, expiry, or analytics; the identity of the link is a product decision, not just an encoding trick.

deepDives.title: 301 versus 302 redirects
points: Use 302 or 307 when the destination may change, because clients and intermediaries should not cache the mapping as permanently; use 301 only for intentionally immutable links.
Redirect status and Cache-Control headers affect how quickly updates, deletion, and revocation take effect, so cache policy belongs in the lifecycle design.
Analytics should describe the redirect decision and accepted event, not depend on the browser making a second request or on a synchronous analytics write.

deepDives.title: Database choice and access patterns
points: A key-value or wide-column store fits the dominant shortCode-to-URL lookup and horizontal redirect scale; a relational store is attractive when owner queries, transactions, and alias constraints dominate.
Keep the authoritative ShortURL row small and index owner/status/expiry operations separately from the hot redirect key.
Whichever store is chosen, require conditional writes for alias allocation, optimistic version checks for updates, and multi-zone replication for the redirect SLO.

deepDives.title: Caching and cache stampedes
points: Use edge caching plus a regional Redis-style cache-aside layer for active mappings, with TTLs that balance hit rate against revocation speed.
Coalesce concurrent misses, add jitter to expirations, and replicate or isolate exceptionally hot codes so one viral link does not overload one cache shard or origin row.
Negative-cache unknown or disabled codes for a short period, but keep the TTL bounded so a newly created or re-enabled link is not hidden for long.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot links
points: Partition durable lookups by a hash of shortCode rather than raw sequential IDs, which distributes writes and avoids sequential-key hotspots.
A single viral code can still be hot after hashing; absorb it with edge and regional cache replicas, request coalescing, and per-key rate protection.
Keep code allocation and redirect lookup independently scalable because creation volume is much smaller than redirect volume.

deepDives.title: Availability and degraded redirects
points: The redirect path should require only edge/cache and a replicated link store; analytics, dashboards, abuse re-scoring, and cleanup workers must not be synchronous dependencies.
On a regional cache failure, fail over to another cache or the authoritative store with bounded retries and circuit breakers rather than retrying a slow dependency indefinitely.
Do not serve an unbounded stale destination after explicit deletion or disablement; use versioned invalidation and a bounded stale policy.

deepDives.title: Read-after-write and eventual consistency
points: After creating a link, return success only when the authoritative write is committed and the serving region can resolve the new code, or route the first read to that authority.
Use a per-link version or conditional update so cache refreshes cannot overwrite a newer destination with an older one.
Click totals and dashboard dimensions can be eventually consistent as long as the UI exposes a freshness watermark and the raw event stream remains replayable.

deepDives.title: Expiration, updates, and deletion
points: Treat expiration as a serving decision based on expiresAt, with background TTL cleanup as storage maintenance rather than the only enforcement mechanism.
Updates and deletes write the authoritative status first, then invalidate edge and regional caches; tombstones prevent stale replicas from resurrecting a code.
Retain audit and click data only for the configured policy, and make cache invalidation observable so operators can measure revocation delay.

deepDives.title: Abuse, security, and enumeration
points: Allow only supported URL schemes, normalize destinations, scan or score suspicious domains, and provide reporting and takedown controls for phishing or malware.
Rate-limit creation, custom-alias attempts, and redirect abuse separately; do not let a bad destination or bot campaign exhaust the redirect budget for healthy links.
Use opaque codes where privacy matters, avoid exposing sequential volume through the public namespace, and minimize or hash analytics identifiers before retention.

deepDives.title: Asynchronous click analytics
points: Emit a compact ClickEvent after the redirect decision through a durable buffer or queue; the user-visible 302 must not wait for a broker, worker, or analytics database.
Use event IDs and idempotent aggregation so at-least-once delivery does not inflate counts; late events should update a bounded correction window.
Separate raw-event retention from dashboard aggregates and publish processing lag so owners understand when analytics is delayed.

tradeoffs.title: Sequential IDs versus random codes
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use a unique ID plus Base62 for compact capacity, then add an opaque permutation or random allocation when enumeration resistance is a stronger requirement.
tradeoffs.caution: Purely sequential public codes reveal volume and can create hot allocation patterns; purely random codes require collision checks and retries.

tradeoffs.title: 301 versus 302 by link lifecycle
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use 302 or 307 for mutable links and 301 for links explicitly declared immutable, with cache headers that match revocation expectations.
tradeoffs.caution: Permanent caching improves repeat latency but makes destination updates and deletion harder to propagate quickly.

tradeoffs.title: Key-value store versus relational database
tradeoffs.recommendation: Choose a key-value store when shortCode lookup and scale dominate; choose relational storage when owner workflows, transactions, and reporting relationships justify it.
tradeoffs.caution: A key-value design needs deliberate secondary indexes and management queries, while a relational design needs careful partitioning and read replicas at redirect scale.

tradeoffs.title: Cache TTL versus immediate revocation
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use cache-aside TTLs with targeted invalidation and a versioned status check for updates, deletes, and abuse takedowns.
tradeoffs.caution: Long TTLs improve hit rate but extend stale-destination risk; short TTLs reduce that risk at the cost of origin load.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous versus asynchronous click logging
tradeoffs.recommendation: Buffer click events and process them asynchronously so redirect availability and latency remain independent of analytics health.
tradeoffs.caution: Async processing can delay or correct totals, so the product must expose freshness and accept at-least-once aggregation semantics.

commonMistakes: Treating availability, traffic, latency, and code length as interchangeable scale assumptions.
Generating aliases without a uniqueness constraint, collision strategy, or idempotency boundary.
Putting a database or analytics transaction on every redirect without a cache-first or degraded path.
Caching a redirect forever without an expiration, version, or revocation policy.
Allowing open redirects or malicious destinations without validation, reporting, and rate limits.
Treating analytics aggregates as exact source-of-truth events or allowing duplicate queue delivery to inflate counts.

followUps.question: What if two requests choose the same custom alias?
followUps.answer: Reserve the alias with a conditional uniqueness write, return a conflict to the losing request, and make a retry with the same idempotency key return the original link.

followUps.question: How do you handle a viral short code?
followUps.answer: Replicate the mapping at the edge and regional caches, coalesce origin misses, and isolate per-code traffic so one hot key does not overload a cache shard or database partition.

followUps.question: How do you revoke a link quickly?
followUps.answer: Write a disabled or tombstone state first, invalidate edge and regional caches, and keep a bounded cache TTL and version check so stale destinations cannot persist indefinitely.

followUps.question: What happens when analytics is down?
followUps.answer: Return the redirect, buffer or durably queue the click event when possible, alert on queue lag, and show a delayed analytics watermark instead of blocking healthy redirect traffic.

rubric.description: The answer separates create and redirect traffic, states traffic, latency, availability, retention, and code-space assumptions, and defines lifecycle and abuse behavior.
The answer makes ShortURL authority, shortCode lookup, ownership, status, expiry, versioning, idempotency, click events, and rebuildable aggregates explicit.
The answer uses cache-first redirects, hashed partitions, hot-code isolation, bounded retries, and independently scalable asynchronous analytics.
The answer covers read-after-write creation, conditional updates, cache invalidation, degraded redirects, multi-zone state, replay, and observable freshness.
The candidate can explain code allocation, redirect status, database choice, cache policy, revocation, and why analytics stays off the critical path.
